scope_decision.preservation_policy: Do not delete, disable, simplify, or weaken existing PSO/BND implementation, source artifacts, fixtures, tests, audit contracts or unresolved-result behavior. Preserve future-class requirements and evidence in this overlay.

profiles.description: VCF carrying called variants for germline SNV and short-indel reanalysis; no reference-confidence block interpretation.
profiles.mode_selection: Explicit persisted input mode. Auto-detection may suggest a mode but must not silently reinterpret an ambiguous file.
critical_controls: Treat '*' spanning-deletion ALT as a distinct VCF allele token, not a sequence allele and not the '<*>' unknown allele.
Recognize '<NON_REF>' and '<*>' as reference-confidence constructs; route to gVCF mode or an explicit unsupported-input path, never treat them as ordinary clinical ALT alleles.
Normalize only called sequence alleles against the selected operational FASTA; do not normalize or split reference-confidence blocks.
Preserve original record, original allele indexes, all sample genotypes and field values, and a reversible original-to-normalized mapping.
A mixed file containing in-scope small variants and out-of-scope SV/BND/CNV/repeat records requires explicit partial-processing policy and durable per-record routing; no silent record loss.
VCFv4.0 remains blocked from source-qualified acceptance until exact historical source provenance is pinned.
profiles.source_version_policy: Retain VCFv4.0–4.5 source research. Apply only version-confirmed semantics. VCFv4.0 has a source-provenance blocker; do not claim its normative conformance.

profiles.description: Germline VCF containing called variants plus sample-level reference-confidence blocks. Blocks are coverage/confidence evidence, not ordinary variant alleles or proof of a clinical reference genotype outside their covered interval.
profiles.mode_selection: Explicit persisted input mode and producer/dialect profile. Do not infer producer conventions from fileformat version alone.
critical_controls: Separate VCF core semantics from producer-specific GATK gVCF conventions.
VCFv4.1/4.2 have no dedicated gVCF reference-block section in the reviewed core sources; GATK-style <NON_REF>/END behavior needs an independently pinned producer dialect.
VCFv4.3/4.4 reference-only blocks use the INFO/END-based model and <*>; the source crosswalk records <*> as preferred over <NON_REF>.
VCFv4.5 introduces sample-specific FORMAT/LEN behavior, per-sample implicit-call restrictions and the LAA exception; do not back-apply this model to VCFv4.3/4.4.
When VCFv4.5 LEN is present, preserve sample-specific block lengths. END inference is a backward-compatibility SHOULD, not a universal replacement for LEN.
At implicitly called positions, enforce missing GT and the FORMAT-field restriction; when LAA is present at a block start, include <*> for that sample.
Process each sample's block extent independently; do not treat a shared INFO/END as proof that all samples have identical block boundaries.
Reference blocks are not variant records and must not enter the SNV/indel normalization or pathogenicity scoring path.
Gaps in reference-confidence blocks remain no-call/insufficient-coverage evidence, not benign evidence.
GATK GQ-band conventions and exact producer behavior require pinned producer/version sources and real producer fixtures.
VCFv4.0 remains blocked from source-qualified acceptance until exact historical source provenance is pinned.
profiles.source_version_policy: Retain VCFv4.0–4.5 core source research and add a separate producer-dialect registry for GATK-style gVCF. VCFv4.0–4.2 gVCF support is not source-qualified by the VCF core documents alone; VCFv4.3/4.4 use END-based blocks; VCFv4.5 uses sample-specific LEN/implicit-position rules.

source_gap_candidates.finding: The canonical 226 ledger does not contain atomic requirements for the VCFv4.3/4.4 reference-only block model using INFO/END and <*> (with <*> preferred over <NON_REF>).
source_gap_candidates.next_action: Extract each normative obligation with complete source context, exact modality, and version applicability; map to tests.

source_gap_candidates.finding: The VCFv4.1/4.2 core sources reviewed contain no dedicated gVCF reference-block section. GATK-style <NON_REF>/END reference-confidence blocks therefore require a separately pinned GATK producer convention, not a fabricated VCF-core requirement.
source_gap_candidates.next_action: Pin exact GATK documentation/source and producer versions; define supported GATK gVCF dialects, including END, NON_REF, PL and GQ-band conventions; add real producer fixtures.

source_gap_candidates.finding: The 226 ledger has a reserved FORMAT/LEN field-definition row (VCF-REQ-000169) and an END-to-LEN inference candidate (VCF-REQ-000129), but no complete atomic set for sample-specific block lengths, mixed sample block extents, and all boundary cases.
source_gap_candidates.next_action: Decompose sample-specific LEN and END inference rules, mixed variant/reference records, and sample-level interval behavior into atomic requirements.

source_gap_candidates.finding: VCF-REQ-000126/127 cover implicit-position GT/FORMAT restrictions and LAA inclusion, but no complete executable conformance evidence is mapped.
source_gap_candidates.next_action: Add mixed-sample positive/negative/boundary fixtures for missing GT, only-LAA exception, LAA containing <*> at block start, and implicit positions.

source_gap_candidates.finding: VCF-REQ-000128 records the VCFv4.5 backward-compatibility alias as RECOMMENDED/APPLICABLE only in 4.5. Earlier GATK <NON_REF> behavior is a producer convention and must not be generalized as a VCF-core MUST.
source_gap_candidates.next_action: Keep VCFv4.5 alias force exact; add a separate GATK dialect mapping for earlier versions after source pinning.

source_gap_candidates.finding: No dedicated canonical requirement explicitly separates the '*' spanning-deletion allele from <*> unknown/reference-confidence allele and ordinary sequence ALT alleles.
source_gap_candidates.next_action: Extract source clauses and add genotype/allele-index tests proving '*' is retained as a spanning-deletion placeholder, not normalized as a sequence allele or conflated with <*>.

source_gap_candidates.finding: The small-variant source crosswalk identifies an explicit increasing-POS sorting requirement added in VCFv4.3, but this clause is not represented as a dedicated canonical requirement in the 226 ledger.
source_gap_candidates.next_action: Verify complete version context and add version-specific ordering tests; do not back-project the 4.3 clause to 4.1/4.2 without source evidence.
